name: Nicolae Rainea
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Rainea played lower-league football until retiring in 1959 (age 26), then became a referee; his Liga I debut came in November 1965 at age 32, and he made the FIFA list in 1967 at age 34.
early_history_summary: Rainea played football in the lower leagues of Romania for several clubs before retiring as a player in 1959 to begin a refereeing career. family_context_summary: Rainea worked at a ball-bearing factory in Bârlad for 32 years while refereeing, suggesting a working-class background with no special financial platform.
evidence_summary: Rainea's refereeing career began only after he retired from lower-league playing at age 26 in 1959. His first-division debut was in 1965 at age 32, and he joined the FIFA list in 1967. No material milestone by age 26 is documented.

name: Boris Shakhlin
milestone_by_age_26: Won team gold and horizontal bar silver at the 1954 World Championships in Rome at age 22, followed by the 1955 European Championship title and two gold medals at the 1956 Olympics.
early_history_summary: Shakhlin began gymnastics at age 12 in 1944 in Ishim, Siberia, after his father's death left him orphaned and raised by his grandmother. He became champion of his town at 14, transferred to Sverdlovsk at 17, and was sent to Kiev at 19 to train under coach Alexander Mishakov at the Kiev Institute of Physical Culture. By 22 he was competing at the World Championships.
family_context_summary: Born in Ishim, Siberia; father was a railway worker who died in 1944, leaving Boris and his elder brother to be raised by their grandmother in modest circumstances.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no evidence of family gymnastics background.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Soviet sports system, Mishakov coaching, orphaned early, Kiev Institute
evidence_summary: Orphaned at 12 when his railway-worker father died, Shakhlin was raised by his grandmother in Siberia and channeled his energy into gymnastics. The Soviet sports pipeline identified him early: he was moved from Ishim to Sverdlovsk to Kiev, where coach Alexander Mishakov and training partner Viktor Chukarin accelerated his development. By 22 he won team gold at the 1954 World Championships, and by 24 he was an Olympic champion. The adversity of orphanhood and the elite Soviet gymnastics ecosystem were the dominant early advantages.
starting_point: Born in 1932 in Ishim, Siberia; father was a railway worker who died in 1944, leaving Boris and his elder brother to be raised by their grandmother in modest circumstances.
current_position: Died on 30 May 2008 in Kyiv, Ukraine at age 76; final role was lecturer at the University of Kyiv and former FIG Men's Technical Committee member.

trajectory.event: Won team gold and horizontal bar silver at the World Championships in Rome, placing fourth all-around.
Won the European Championships in Frankfurt, earning the nickname 'The Russian Bear' from German journalists.
Won Olympic gold medals in pommel horse and team competition at the Melbourne Olympics.
Dominated the World Championships in Moscow with five gold medals.
Became Olympic all-around champion in Rome, winning seven total medals at the 1960 Games.
Retired from competition after suffering a heart attack.
Died on 30 May 2008 in Kyiv, Ukraine.

name: Eugen Doga
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Doga was studying cello at the Chișinău Conservatory (1955-1960) and working as a cellist in the Moldovan State Television and Radio orchestra from 1957. His composition debut (a string quartet) came in 1963 at age 26, but his major works and fame arrived in the 1970s-1980s.
early_history_summary: Doga walked barefoot from his village to Chișinău to enroll in music school despite no prior training. He studied cello (1951-1955) and then at the Conservatory (1955-1960). Left-hand paralysis ended his cello career, prompting him to study composition (1960-1965). He worked as a cellist and teacher while composing.
family_context_summary: Born in the village of Mocra in Rîbnița District, Moldova, to a Romanian family; came from poverty, walking barefoot to Chișinău to attend music school.
evidence_summary: Doga's early career was as a cellist and student; his first composition (a string quartet) debuted in 1963 at age 26, which is not a material milestone. His fame came from film scores and ballets in the 1970s-1980s, well after age 26.

name: Vreni Schneider
milestone_by_age_26: Won her first World Cup race in December 1984 at age 20, and by age 26 had won two Olympic gold medals (1988 Calgary), two World Championship golds (1987, 1989), and set a single-season record of 14 World Cup wins in 1988-89.
early_history_summary: Schneider grew up in Elm, a small Swiss Alpine village, the daughter of a shoemaker. She started skiing at age three and was competing by first grade. Her mother died of cancer when Vreni was about 16, causing her to pause her ski career and drop out of school to manage the household. She resumed skiing and made her World Cup debut in December 1984 at age 20, winning immediately.
family_context_summary: Daughter of a village shoemaker in Elm, Glarus, Switzerland; mother died of cancer when Schneider was a teenager, forcing her to put skiing on hold and drop out of school to care for the family home.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; father was a shoemaker, no evidence of skiing background in the family.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Swiss Alps village, ski club Elm, early skiing from age 3, mother's death
evidence_summary: Schneider's dominant early advantage was growing up in Elm, a Swiss Alpine village where skiing was the local culture. She started at age three and was competing by first grade, giving her deep domain proximity. Her mother's death when she was 16 created adversity that paused but did not derail her career. The Swiss national ski pipeline provided institutional support, and she won her first World Cup race at 20, going on to become the most successful Swiss alpine skier ever.
starting_point: Born in 1964 in Elm, Glarus, Switzerland; daughter of a village shoemaker, youngest of four children; mother died of cancer when Vreni was about 16.
current_position: Retired from competitive skiing in 1995; runs a ski and snowboard school and sports shop in her home village of Elm, Switzerland; voted Swiss Sportswoman of the Century.

trajectory.event: Made World Cup debut and won her first World Cup race (giant slalom) in December 1984.
Won World Championship gold in giant slalom at Crans-Montana, Switzerland.
Won two Olympic gold medals (slalom and giant slalom) at the Calgary Winter Olympics.
Won World Championship gold in giant slalom at Vail and set a single-season record of 14 World Cup wins.
Won Olympic slalom gold and silver in combined at the Lillehammer Winter Olympics.
Retired from competitive skiing after winning her third overall World Cup title.

name: Vladimir Dzhanibekov
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Dzhanibekov graduated from the Higher Military Fighter Pilot School in Yeysk in 1965 (age 23) and was working as a pilot-instructor. He was selected as a cosmonaut in April 1970 at age 28, and his first space flight was in January 1978 at age 36.
early_history_summary: Dzhanibekov studied at the Tashkent Suvorov military school before graduating from the Higher Military Fighter Pilot School in Yeysk in 1965. He worked as a pilot-instructor until being selected for cosmonaut training in 1970. His first space mission did not occur until 1978.
family_context_summary: Born in Iskandar, Uzbek SSR; attended Tashkent Suvorov military school, suggesting a military-oriented upbringing.
evidence_summary: Dzhanibekov was a military pilot and instructor through his twenties; cosmonaut selection came at 28 and first spaceflight at 36. No material milestone by age 26 is documented.

name: Li Hongzhi
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Li worked on a PLA stud farm at 17 and later as a trumpet player in a police band, guesthouse attendant, and grain store clerk through his twenties. He founded Falun Gong in 1992 at approximately age 40-41.
early_history_summary: Li Hongzhi was born in Jilin province, China. State media reports describe an unexceptional student whose only talent was playing the trumpet. He worked on a People's Liberation Army stud farm at 17, then as a trumpeter in a police band, guesthouse attendant, and grain store clerk before beginning qigong study around 1988 and founding Falun Gong in 1992.
family_context_summary: Born in Gongzhuling, Jilin Province, China; one account states the family lived amidst poverty. Competing biographical accounts exist between supporters and detractors.
evidence_summary: Li's early life was unremarkable according to available sources; he held menial jobs through his twenties and only began studying qigong around 1988. Falun Gong was founded in 1992 when Li was approximately 40. No material milestone by age 26 is documented.

name: Aurelio De Laurentiis
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. De Laurentiis co-founded the production company Filmauro with his father Luigi in 1975 at age 26, but the company's first major box office success came in 1980 with 'Qua la mano' when he was 31. His significant commercial achievements and Napoli football club acquisition came later.
early_history_summary: De Laurentiis was born into Italian film industry royalty as the nephew of producer Dino De Laurentiis and son of Luigi De Laurentiis. He co-founded Filmauro with his father in 1975, leveraging the family's film business connections. However, the company's first major hit did not arrive until 1980.
family_context_summary: Born in Rome to Luigi De Laurentiis, a film producer; nephew of famed producer Dino De Laurentiis. The De Laurentiis family is Italian film industry royalty with deep roots in Naples and Torre Annunziata.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Luigi De Laurentiis was a film producer; uncle Dino De Laurentiis was a major Hollywood and Italian film producer. The family business provided direct industry immersion from childhood.
evidence_summary: While De Laurentiis had extraordinary family advantages in the film industry, founding Filmauro at 26 with his father was not a material milestone in itself. His first commercial success came at 31 in 1980, and his most notable achievements (Napoli acquisition, major hits) came even later. No material milestone by age 26 is documented.

name: Lasse Hallström
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Hallström made short pop music clips for Swedish television from the late 1960s and sold a short documentary to TV at 16, but his first credited directorial work (TV series 'Pappas pojkar') came in 1973 at age 27, and his first feature film was in 1975 at age 29. His international breakthrough came with 'My Life as a Dog' in 1985 at age 39.
early_history_summary: Hallström grew up in Stockholm with a dentist father who was an amateur filmmaker and a mother who was an author and poet. He made 8mm films as a child and sold a short pop documentary to Swedish TV at 16. He spent about 10 years making short film inserts for Swedish television before his first credited directorial work in 1973.
family_context_summary: Born in Stockholm, Sweden; father was a dentist and keen amateur videographer who won a prize for a short film; mother was the author and poet Karin Lyberg. Middle-class creative household with early filmmaking exposure.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father's passion for amateur filmmaking directly inspired Lasse's early interest in film; father won a first prize in DN for the color film 'Sommarstad' in 1939. Mother was a published author and poet.
evidence_summary: Hallström had early creative advantages from his father's amateur filmmaking and his mother's literary background, and he was making TV content from his early twenties. However, his first credited directorial work was at 27 and his first feature film at 29. No specific material milestone by age 26 is documented.

name: Anastasia Baburova
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Baburova was a journalism student at Moscow State University and freelance journalist who contributed to Novaya Gazeta from October 2008. She was assassinated on January 19, 2009 at age 25. Her notability derives from her murder, not from a career achievement by age 26.
early_history_summary: Baburova was born in Sevastopol and studied management and international law before switching to journalism at Moscow State University in 2004. She worked as a freelance journalist for several Russian outlets and joined Novaya Gazeta in October 2008, covering neo-Nazi groups. She was shot and killed alongside human rights lawyer Stanislav Markelov in January 2009.
family_context_summary: Born in Sevastopol, Ukrainian SSR; details of family background not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Baburova was a student and beginning freelance journalist who was tragically assassinated at 25. Her notability comes from her murder, not from any career milestone achieved by age 26. No material milestone by age 26 is documented.

name: Bob Hewitt
milestone_by_age_26: Won his first Grand Slam title at the 1961 Australian Championships in mixed doubles at age 21, followed by Wimbledon men's doubles titles in 1962 and 1964 and Australian Open men's doubles titles in 1963 and 1964, all before age 26.
early_history_summary: Hewitt was born in Dubbo, New South Wales, Australia, and began playing tennis as an amateur from 1958 at age 18. He reached the Australian Open singles semifinals in 1960 at age 20, and won his first Grand Slam title in mixed doubles at the 1961 Australian Championships. He formed a dominant doubles partnership with Fred Stolle, winning multiple Grand Slam titles in the early 1960s.
family_context_summary: Born in Dubbo, a regional town approximately 400 km northwest of Sydney, Australia. Family financial background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Australian tennis system, Fred Stolle doubles partnership, early Grand Slam titles
evidence_summary: Hewitt emerged from regional Australia into the strong Australian tennis ecosystem of the late 1950s and 1960s. His most significant early advantage was his doubles partnership with Fred Stolle, with whom he won multiple Grand Slam titles starting at age 21. The Australian tennis infrastructure provided competitive depth and pathway access. Family background details are not documented in reviewed sources. He later moved to South Africa and was convicted of rape in 2015, for which he was expelled from the Tennis Hall of Fame.
starting_point: Born in 1940 in Dubbo, New South Wales, Australia, a regional town about 400 km from Sydney; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Convicted of rape and sexual assault in 2015; sentenced to six years in prison; paroled in 2020; expelled from the International Tennis Hall of Fame in 2016; resides in Eastern Cape, South Africa.

name: K. C. Nicolaou
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Nicolaou completed his BSc in 1969 (age 23) and his PhD in 1972 (age 26) at the University of London. His postdoctoral work at Columbia and Harvard followed, and his first independent faculty appointment came in 1976 at age 30. His landmark total synthesis work came later in his career.
early_history_summary: Nicolaou was born in Karavas, Cyprus, and was inspired by a high school chemistry teacher at age 15. He emigrated to England in 1964 at age 18, spent two years learning English, then earned his BSc at Bedford College (1969) and PhD at University College London (1972). He completed postdocs at Columbia and Harvard under E.J. Corey before joining the University of Pennsylvania faculty in 1976.
family_context_summary: Born in Karavas, a small coastal town in northern Cyprus; emigrated to England at 18 to pursue chemistry, spending two years learning English before entering university.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; inspired by a high school chemistry teacher in Nicosia, not by family.
evidence_summary: Nicolaou's PhD completion at age 26 is a standard academic credential, not a material milestone. His significant scientific contributions (total synthesis of Taxol, calicheamicin, etc.) and independent career began after age 30. No material milestone by age 26 is documented.

name: Yvonne Rüegg
milestone_by_age_26: Won the gold medal in giant slalom at the 1960 Winter Olympics in Squaw Valley at age 21, and was Swiss national champion in downhill in 1959 at age 20.
early_history_summary: Rüegg was born in Chur, Switzerland, and was a member of Ski Club Arosa. She won the Swiss national downhill championship in 1959 at age 20, then achieved her career-defining result by winning the Olympic gold medal in giant slalom at the 1960 Winter Olympics in Squaw Valley, narrowly beating American Penny Pitou by one-tenth of a second.
family_context_summary: Born in Chur, Switzerland; her aunt Anny Rüegg attended the 1936 Winter Olympics as an alpine skier for Switzerland, suggesting a family connection to competitive skiing.
parent_family_domain_summary: Aunt Anny Rüegg was an alpine skier who attended the 1936 Winter Olympics for Switzerland, providing a family precedent in the sport.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Swiss Alps, Ski Club Arosa, aunt Olympic skier, 1960 Olympic gold
evidence_summary: Rüegg's early advantage was growing up in Switzerland's Alpine skiing culture, with the Ski Club Arosa as her training base. Her aunt Anny Rüegg had attended the 1936 Olympics as a skier, providing a family precedent. She won the Swiss national downhill title at 20 and Olympic gold in giant slalom at 21. The 1960 Olympic gold was her only major international success, after which she married Italian skier Roberto Siorpaes. Detailed family financial information is not documented.
starting_point: Born in 1938 in Chur, Switzerland; aunt Anny Rüegg was an Olympic alpine skier, suggesting a family with skiing tradition.
current_position: Retired from competitive skiing; married Italian skier Roberto Siorpaes; later life details not widely documented.
